text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Bill Clinton has stressed the importance of Asia to the United States, saying that "Asia's stability affects our peace".
- Cases of measles in Singapore have risen sharply, with more than 700 reported in the first five months of this year.
- Parliament begins its debate on the President's Address on Monday.

- Singapore labour union chief Lim Boon Heng calls on all businesses to "exercise moderation" in price hikes, following the National Wages Council's recommendations for moderate wage increases this year.
- Singapore's per capita gross domestic product (GDP) could surpass the US$30,000 mark this year, exceeding the GDPs in leading world economies such as the United States and Germany.
- Singapore Airlines will resume talks with Air-India this month on a variety of issues that go beyond code-sharing and marketing arrangements.

- Japan's Finance Ministry is preparing to shut down Nomura Securities Co's head office and some of its branches for up to six months as one of the country's biggest finance scandals escalates, a national newspaper said.

- National Computer Systems, a subsidiary of the National Computer Board and one of Singapore's biggest information technology companies, is to be sold by private tender to a government-linked company.

- Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar are among the most attractive currencies in the world, according to a ranking of 54 currencies by London-based Cross Border Capital (CBC), an asset allocation adviser.

- Owners of Housing Board flats can upgrade to new executive condominiums (ECs) after five years and not have to meet the new 10-year waiting period -- but only if they buy ECs in the "open category".
- Electronics contract manufacturer Venture Manufacturing looks forward to another promising year and could well be on an acquisition trail with its cash hoard of over Singapore $100 million.
- Singatronics, known generally as an electronics counter, is slowly but surely building up a hotel and property portfolio Down Under.
